chunks: 1536 - And it is narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan, meaning Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: “What is there for one who performs the Salat of Jaʿfar?” He said: “If he had sins like the sand of ʿĀlij and the foam of the sea, Allah would forgive them for him.” He said: I said, “Is this for us?” He said: “For whom would it be except for you specifically?”
He said: I said, “Then what should I recite in it?” He said—and I said, “Shall I recite various parts of the Qur’an?”—he said:
“No; recite in it: ‘When the earth is shaken,’ and ‘When the help of Allah comes,’ and ‘Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of al-Qadr,’ and ‘Say: He is Allah, One.’”

key_terms.أَعْتَرِضُ الْقُرْآنَ: To recite from various parts of the Qur’an.
key_terms.إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ: Sūrat al-Naṣr, one of the surahs prescribed in this prayer.
key_terms.إِذَا زُلْزِلَتْ: Sūrat al-Zalzalah, one of the surahs prescribed in this prayer.
key_terms.ذُنُوبًا: Sins for which forgiveness is promised through this act of worship.
key_terms.رَمْلِ عَالِجٍ: A metaphor for an immense quantity, referring to the sand of ʿĀlij.
key_terms.زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ: The foam of the sea, used to indicate a vast number of sins.
key_terms.صَلَاةَ جَعْفَرٍ: The special prayer attributed to Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib.
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, one of the surahs prescribed in this prayer.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of Salat Jaʿfar and which surahs are recited in it?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the immense reward of Salat Jaʿfar, stating that Allah forgives even an immense abundance of sins for the one who performs it. It also gives practical guidance on what to recite in this prayer, specifying four surahs from the Qur’an.
